destinations.title: How does a P^2 hybrid base change characteristic widths and logarithmic distance scales relative to P^1 hybrids?
How far can scalar fields move in an unstabilized Calabi–Yau vector-multiplet moduli space before its effective description changes substantially?
Does the finite-width and logarithmic-distance pattern persist in a second two-parameter model with P^1 and orbifold hybrids?
Do characteristic non-geometric excursions and logarithmic distance scales remain of order the Planck scale in the studied Calabi–Yau moduli spaces?
Can many small non-geometric regions combine into a parametrically large pre-asymptotic geodesic excursion as moduli count increases?
Can characteristic LG excursions remain small when many moduli are available, and what can a symmetry-restricted calculation establish?

Can a finite non-geometric phase provide a large proper displacement before the exponential mass decrease associated with large volume becomes relevant? The paper follows trajectories from such phases toward infinite-distance regions.
How do proper distances behave across geometric, LG, and hybrid regimes in a two-complex-dimensional Calabi–Yau moduli space?

What happens to the spectrum when scalar moduli traverse parametrically large proper distances? The conjecture predicts exponentially descending towers, so the low-energy spectrum cannot remain fixed throughout the limit.

How can an EFT fail near a moduli-space boundary when its leading metric remains accurate? The caption distinguishes ordinary corrections that limit a local patch from a tower-induced quantum-gravity cutoff that falls toward an infinite-distance singularity.
Do geodesics from exotic finite-distance pseudo-hybrid limits toward large volume satisfy the refined swampland distance conjecture (RSDC), including examples arising from non-abelian GLSMs?

Does a large geodesic displacement in moduli space require an exponentially light tower? The reviewed distinction is between an asymptotic prediction and onset already at distances of order M_P, with an order-one exponential coefficient.

Does the refined Distance Conjecture constrain low-energy physics in finite regions of moduli space, and can alternative refinements impose absolute bounds on tower masses rather than merely relative exponential suppression?

Which geometric and spectral conditions connect the local Tower Scalar Weak Gravity Conjecture to the asymptotic Sharpened Distance Conjecture when moduli spaces are curved and scalar-charge-to-mass vectors vary with moduli?

When do compactifiability and assumptions on the spectrum imply the Swampland Distance Conjecture (SDC) for locally symmetric moduli spaces, and how do Lie-group weights determine leading towers and their decay rates?
